_comment: WHY EACH COMMAND LOOKS LIKE THIS.
1. THE INTERPRETER IS RESOLVED, NOT NAMED. These read `python3` only. That is the
right name on most Linux and macOS installs and the wrong one on Windows and on
any environment where the interpreter is `python`. Because the whole command is
guarded with `|| exit 0`, a missing `python3` did not error — the hook silently
did nothing, which is the worst failure a guard can have. `command -v python3 ||
command -v python` tries both.
2. IT FAILS OPEN, ON PURPOSE. No interpreter, or laserbrain not installed, exits 0
and permits the call. A hook that denies because it could not load itself would
brick every tool call in the session. Verified: exit 0 in both cases.
3. THE IMPORT PROBE IS A SEPARATE SPAWN, ALSO ON PURPOSE. Running the module
directly would print a ModuleNotFoundError traceback into the host's stderr on
every single tool call for anyone who installed the plugin without the package.
Redirecting the real run's stderr instead would silence lb_gate's own warnings,
which travel on stderr by design.
4. lb_safety IS HERE. It was missing until 2026-08-29, so everyone who installed
this plugin got the coverage gate and no destructive-command guard. It is the
hook that refuses `rm -rf`, force pushes and the like. Shipping the gate that
governs goal drift while omitting the one that governs destruction is the wrong
half to leave out.
5. DENIAL DOES NOT TRAVEL BY EXIT CODE. It is stdout JSON —
hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision — so `|| exit 0` cannot suppress a real
block. See lb_gate.py:712.

hooks.command: LB_PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) && [ -n "$LB_PY" ] && "$LB_PY" -c 'import laserbrain' 2>/dev/null && LASERBRAIN_AGENT=claude "$LB_PY" -m laserbrain.hooks.lb_gate || exit 0
LB_PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) && [ -n "$LB_PY" ] && "$LB_PY" -c 'import laserbrain' 2>/dev/null && LASERBRAIN_AGENT=claude "$LB_PY" -m laserbrain.hooks.lb_safety || exit 0
LB_PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) && [ -n "$LB_PY" ] && "$LB_PY" -c 'import laserbrain' 2>/dev/null && LASERBRAIN_AGENT=claude "$LB_PY" -m laserbrain.hooks.lb_coverage || exit 0
LB_PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) && [ -n "$LB_PY" ] && "$LB_PY" -c 'import laserbrain' 2>/dev/null && LASERBRAIN_AGENT=claude "$LB_PY" -m laserbrain.hooks.lb_coverage || exit 0
